replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper6534 by Reviewer qbyu

content.title: Response to Reviewer qbyu
content.comment:
Many thanks for the detailed and constructive review! We appreciate your positive feedback about our paper's motivation and novelty. Here, we address your main concerns:

**Q1: For the process of PPAT, it is better to add figures to illustrate visually the node's inputs and outputs.**

A1: We appreciate your insightful suggestion. However, we cannot add more graphs due to page limit, but we have added more statements about the input and the output in Sec. 3.2.1 (highlighted in blue). We hope these additional explanations address your concern.

**Q2: The reason why design this pairwise self-attention mechanism should be explained.**

A2: While previous work has used vanilla GAT, we apply a simple yet effective approach to **attend to reasoning chains**, more suitable for **causality propagation**. According to the pairwise attention mechanism, **the conclusion node now attends to all possible premise node pairs**, instead of individual nodes. This design is "practically performant and explainable" [JG9h] according to the ablation study (Sec. 4.5) and case study (Sec. 4.6).

**Q3: Detail about input length limitation of BERT and Longformer.**

A3: As stated in Sec. 3.1, we apply a **sentence-level dynamic window** to encode the entire document, and we set the number of sentences in the window at 5 for BERT and 7 for Longformer. For BERT, the length of 5 continuous sentences tokenized by BERT tokenizer is no more than 320, so we set the max length of input tokens at 320. The max length of 512 for Longformer is set in the same way. We have added the above detail in the "implementation detail" section.

**Q4: It's better to add more experiments on similar tasks based on the changes of graph structure.**

A4: Thank you for the insightful suggestion. Our idea of "from intra-sentence to inter-sentence" is indeed "straightforward" [eFfp] and generalizable, yet we propose the sentence boundary event relational graph and information propagation through reasoning chains, **specifically designed for causality prediction**. We will consider extending PPAT to identification of other event relations in future work, especially the implicit relations in need of reasoning.

**Q5: For reproducibility, the construction of the graph should be introduced in detail. In addition, it is better to open source the codes.**

A5: Thanks for the suggestion. We have added more explanations about the construction of the graph in Sec. 1 with an example (highlighted in blue). In addition, we have uploaded our code in the supplementary material for reproducibility.

We hope the above details and the general response have addressed your concerns. We are greatful for your help in improving the paper. If there are any additional questions or concerns, we are happy to engage in further discussions.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper explores a method for event causality identification that aims to predict the causal relation between a pair of events mentioned in text. The key ideas of the method involve the dependence of inter-sentence causal reasoning on intra-sentence causal prediction while intra-sentence causal reasoning can be sufficiently done with sentence context (i.e., no interaction with inter-sentence prediction). The paper also considers reasoning chains (i.e., premise node pair) that can facilitate causal prediction of challenging inter-sentence event pairs based on predictions for two related and easy pairs. As such, the paper introduces a progressive reasoning component to first perform causal prediction for intra-sentence pairs, and then predict inter-sentence causality based on intra-sentence prediction information. The paper also presents a pairwise attention module to aggregate neighbors at a reasoning chain level for the attention network. Finally, the model involves a causality-guided learning strategy to supervise representations at every layer based on causal labels. Experiments on two datasets show competitive performance of the method over several baselines. The paper also performs ablation study, case study, and representation visualization to better demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

+The paper studies an important problem that is less studied compared to other NLP tasks.

+The method achieves strong performance on two benchmark datasets that can be used as a good baseline for future work.

Weakness:

-A major concern for the paper is the incremental nature/limited novelty of the proposed method. The progressive reasoning component is quite straightforward while the pairwise attention component and its motivation seem to be an incremental extension of the graph-based model in ERGO.

-The paper only evaluates the method on one task of event causality identification. It might be helpful if the model is evaluated on more similar tasks, e.g., event coreference resolution or event argument prediction, to demonstrate the generalization and be more suitable for ICLR.

-There are some details which are unclear in the paper. Please see below.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
-In Equation (11), does it imply that the representations in the last layer are also used to predict intra-sentence causality? If so, the intra-sentence prediction still seems to depend on inter-sentence information in the designed model.

-In Equation (9), is it computed differently for intra-sentence and inter-sentence pairs or is it computed at all for intra-sentence cases? In particular, do the representations for intra-sentence pairs attend to inter-sentence pairs in this computation? This seems important to make sure the model follows the original motivation with the independence of intra-sentence causality from inter-sentence causality.

-The sentence boundary relational event graph is defined at the beginning of Section 3.2.1, but it is unclear how it is used in the graph pairwise attention. It seems that the pairwise attention doesn't need the graph to operate.

content.title: Response to Reviewer eFfp
content.comment:
Thanks for your time and constructive review! We address your concerns as follows:

**Q1: Limited novelty of the proposed method.**

A1: One of our contributions is **the first method to capture the dependence** of inter-sentence causal reasoning on intra-sentence causality, which has "reasonable" motivation and technical designs [qbyu, JG9h]. 

While the general idea of using GAT to identify causality is not in itself novel, our work has motivated the idea of **aggregating neighbors through reasoning chains**, which is more suitable for causality prediction both conceptually and empirically. This simple yet effective modification is "practically performant and explainable" according to the case study (Sec. 4.6) [JG9h] and has "interesting novelty" [qbyu]. 

**Q2: It might be helpful if the model is evaluated on more similar tasks.**

A2: Thank you for the valuable suggestion. Our idea of "from intra-sentence to inter-sentence" is indeed **"straightforward" and generalizable**, yet we currently focus on ECI and propose message passing on reasoning chains, **specifically designed for causality prediction**. We will consider extending PPAT to identification of other event relations in future work, especially the implicit relations in need of reasoning.

**Q3: Does Eq.11 imply that the representations in the last layer are also used to predict intra-sentence causality?**

A3: Yes, we use representations in the last layer for all nodes' classification. However, the intra-sentence event pair representation in the last layer is the **same** as the one in the first layer. We do **NOT** change intra-sentence representation when updating inter-sentence event pair representation in the last three layers (due to the pairwise attention computation detailed in Q5).

**Q4: Do the representations for intra-sentence pairs attend to inter-sentence pairs in Eq. 9's computation?**

A4: No, intra-sentence causality reasoning does **NOT** rely on inter-sentence nodes, which is implemented by the normalized attention coefficients $\alpha_{ij,k}$ in Eq. 9 (the calculation of $\alpha_{ij,k}$ is detailed in Q5).

**Q5: How does the sentence boundary event relational graph used in graph pairwise attention?**

A5: Sorry about lack of clarity in graph pairwise attention computation. We revise the calculation of attention $\alpha_{ij,k}$ over different reasoning chains in Eq. 7:

$$
\alpha\_{ij,k} =\mathrm{softmax}\_{ij}({\rm atten}\_{ij})=\frac{mask\_{ij,k} \exp ({\rm atten}\_{ij,k})}{\sum\_{z \in \mathcal{N}^{-}\_{ij}} mask\_{ij,z} \exp ({\rm atten}\_{ij,z})}
$$

where $mask_{ij,k}$is attention mask based on the graph edge matrix. $mask_{ij,k}$ **is 1 if the node of** $(event_i , event_j)$ **has edges from the premise node pair, i.e.,** $(event_i, event_k)$ **and** $(event_k, event_j)$.

We leverage the sentence bounday event relational graph (SERG) to **constrain node interaction**. Take Figure 1 as an example, the inter-sentence nodes (in green) cannot pass their message to the intra-sentence node (in blue), **showing the independence** of intra-sentence causality from inter-sentence causality, while the intra-sentence node can propagate its causality to inter-sentence nodes, **following the motivation of progressive reasoning.**

We hope the above response and the general response have addressed your concerns. Thank you again for the comprehensive review to help us refine this paper. Please let us know if there are any additional questions.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes a method for determining whether two event mentions in a document are causally related. As presented in the paper, Event Causality Identification (ECI) is composed of sentence-level ECI (SECI) and document-level ECI (DECI), and the latter is a more difficult task since it involves implicit connections.

To solve the problem, the proposed model PPAT applies a hierarchical Graph Attention Network on edge features. First, the event pair representation is obtained by a single-layer GAT with only intra-sentence relations involved. Then it is transformed into the final embedding through a three-layer GAT with inter-sentence relations. The output hidden states of all GAT layers are constrained by an extra causality-related loss.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Strengths**

- The technical design is reasonable. First, the hierarchical structure helps inter-sentence event causality inference. Second, edge encoding makes it easier to express message passing.

- The model is practically performant and explainable. The progressive reasoning strategy seems to have a sound improvement in performance, referring to Table 3. And the case study shows how classification possibilities vary by GAT layers.  

**Weaknesses**

- The technological novelty seems a little bit limited, especially at a conference focusing on machine learning.

- Though the main and ablated results are superior, the analyses can be strengthened. In the visualization section, it is recommended to present the representation of each GAT layer. Perhaps it is more intuitive to show the change of the inter-sentence representation through the encoding layers.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is well-written and easy to follow. Compared to its previous work ERGO (Chen et al. 2022), the main technical contributions are the substitution from node representations to edge representations in GAT layers and the design of a hierarchical inference model. My overall impression is that PPAT is an effective method but may not be so inspirational to the ICLR community. 

In Eq. 3 and 4, the model concatenates a vector and its normalized linear mapping. It appears redundant since only the length of the vector is introduced as extra information. Does this design refer to some existing work? 

Hyper-parameter lambda is not presented in the paper, which may not be conducive to reproduction.
content.summary_of_the_review: The three technical designs of this work for event causality identification are conceptually reasonable and empirically effective. My main concern is that the novelty seems at the borderline level.

content.title: Response to Reviewer JG9h
content.comment:
We sincerely thank the reviewer for the valuable comments. We are glad that you found our technical designs "conceptually reasonable and empirically effective" and our paper "well-written". Here, we address your main concerns as follows:

**Q1: The technological novelty seems a little bit limited.**

A1: About the novelty, we want to clarify that our work is **the first method in ECI to capture the dependence** of inter-sentence causal reasoning on intra-sentence causal prediction. While previous work has used vanilla GAT to aggregate neighborhood nodes, we use **a simple yet effective technique to attend to reasoning chains**, more suitable for causality propagation. The above core contributions of our approach have "reasonable motivation", and "the novelty is interesting" [qbyu]. 

**Q2: Recommendation about presenting the representation of each GAT layer in the visualization section.**

A2: Thank you for the valuable suggestion! We have presented the representation of every layer in the Appendix of our paper's new version. The visualization further proves that:

1. After intra-sentence reasoning, intra- and inter-sentence nodes are divided into two clusters, and **most intra-sentence nodes that have causality are gathered together**. Inter-sentence causal nodes are scattered since their representations are not updated yet.

2. During the inter-sentence reasoning in the last three layers, intra- and inter-sentence nodes are still clustered into two groups, **but the causal nodes are getting closer to each other**, showing the effectiveness of causality-related representation learning in the global reasoning module.

**Q3: What is the point of concatenating $P^l_{ij}$ computed by Eq.3 in Eq.4?**

A3: Thank you for the thoughtful question. In Eq.3, we apply the same linear network (with parameter $W_{c}$ ) to classify event pair representation of each layer and obtain the **predicted causality possibility** (i.e.$P^l_{ij}$). In our preliminary study, we found that concatenating $P^l_{ij}$ with node representation will often lead to better performance as $P^l_{ij}$ has direct causality information.

**Q4: Hyper-parameter lambda is not presented in the paper.**

A4: We finally set the loss weight in the $l$-th layer (i.e. $\lambda^l$) as follows: 
$\lambda^0=2, \lambda^1=6, \lambda^2=0.1, \lambda^3=0.3$. We search $\lambda^0$ and $\lambda^1$ among the following settings and choose the best one on the development set: 

{$\lambda^0=0.3, \lambda^1=1$ }, {$\lambda^0=1, \lambda^1=3$}, {$\lambda^0=2, \lambda^1=6$}, {$\lambda^0=3, \lambda^1=9$}

We did not specifically tune $\lambda^0$ and $\lambda^1$. We have added more information in the "implemetation detail" section (Sec. 4.2) to facilitate reproduction.

We hope the above response and the general response have addressed your concerns, and we are grateful for your help in improving the paper. Please let us know if you have any further comments!
